title: Rigidified lines extend after removing only codimension at least two in the base
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e$. The addition, inverse and identity are $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume the geometric fibres of $p$ are connected. Let $U\subseteq S$ be a dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], and put $G_U=G\times_SU$. A line means an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]; all module pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $N$ be a line on $G_U$ with a rigidification $r:e_U^*N\simeq\mathcal O_U$. There exist an open $V$ of $S$ with $U\subseteq V$ and containing every point $s$ for which $\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}\leq1$, a line $N_V$ on $G_V$, a rigidification $r_V:e_V^*N_V\simeq\mathcal O_V$, and a rigidification-preserving isomorphism $N_V|_{G_U}\simeq N$. Thus every point of the closed complement $S\setminus V$ has local-ring dimension at least two. No claim that the entire regular locus of $S$ is open is included.

source.place: II 3.2.2--3.2.3, codimension-one reduction; agent spreading formulation of the regular-trait extension argument. Local original WANTED. Compare Deligne, Le lemme de Gabber, Section 4.2, and the existing regular-base rigidified-line extension node.

proof.text: Write $\eta$ for the generic point of $S$ and $Z=S\setminus U$. The generic point exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] and belongs to $U$ because $U$ is nonempty and open in the integral scheme $S$. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], every point of local-ring dimension zero is $\eta$: any other point admits the strict generalization $\eta$. Let $T=\{s\in Z:\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}=1\}$. On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ about $s$, [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes $A$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies its stalk with $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Every ideal of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by the images of generators of its contraction to $A$, so the stalk is Noetherian. For each $s\in T$, its local ring $R_s=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain, so [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes it a DVR. Its fraction field is the function field $K=\kappa(\eta)$: on an integral affine chart this is the identity $\operatorname{Frac}(A_{\mathfrak p})=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Thus the inverse image of $U$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R_s$ is its generic point $\operatorname{Spec}K$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), (5) implies (1); properties.tex Tag 02IZ (lemma-codimension-local-ring); schemes.tex Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: Fix $s\in T$ and an affine open $B_s\ni s$. It is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] the closed set $Z\cap B_s$ has finitely many irreducible components, with generic points supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. A component containing $s$ has generic point $t\in Z$ generalizing $s$. If $t\ne s$, the strict chain $s,t,\eta$ contradicts $\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}=1$ by [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains]. Therefore exactly one component contains $s$, namely $\overline{\{s\}}\cap B_s$. Remove the other finitely many components, and choose an affine neighbourhood $A_s$ of $s$ inside the remaining open. Then $Z\cap A_s=\overline{\{s\}}\cap A_s$, an irreducible closed set with generic point $s$. Every smaller open neighbourhood of $s$ retains this equality.

source.place: Tag 0052 (lemma-Noetherian), finite components; schemes.tex Tag 01IS; properties.tex Tag 02IZ. Affine shrinking uses clause (1) of the cited local-ring limit node.

proof.text:
Consider the directed set of affine open neighbourhoods $W\subseteq A_s$ of $s$, ordered by shrinking. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods], its limit is $\operatorname{Spec}R_s$, each $W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and transition maps are affine. There is a set of indices: these opens are subsets of the underlying set of $A_s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] first to $G_{A_s}\to A_s$, then to its open $G_{U\cap A_s}\to A_s$. It gives
$$G_{R_s}=\varprojlim_W G_W,\qquad G_K=\varprojlim_W G_{U\cap W}.$$
The second equality uses the inverse image of $U$ computed in Step 1. Both systems have affine transitions, as included in that node's statement.

source.place: Tag 0GWT (lemma-morphism-glueing-near-closed-point), proof: local ring as neighbourhood colimit; Tag 01YZ (lemma-scheme-over-limit).

proof.text: We check the finiteness hypotheses for both systems before using descent. The assumed finite presentation of $p$ implies finite type: on affine charts finitely presented algebras are finitely generated, and quasi-compactness is part of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Since $p$ is separated, [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] makes $G_W\to W$ separated of finite type and $G_{R_s}\to\operatorname{Spec}R_s$ of finite type. The base $W$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $G_W$ Noetherian. Its open $G_{U\cap W}$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc], applied to this open immersion and the quasi-compact scheme $G_W$; it is locally Noetherian as an open subscheme. Both $G_W$ and $G_{U\cap W}$ are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. They therefore satisfy every hypothesis of the two affine-limit descent nodes used next. No intersection of base affine opens is being assumed affine.

By the smooth clause of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], $G_{R_s}\to\operatorname{Spec}R_s$ is smooth. It is of finite type by Step 4, so [lem-sfb-smooth-dvr-generic-line-extension] applies to the line $N_K$ on $G_K$ and supplies a line $H_s$ on $G_{R_s}$ and an isomorphism $H_s|_{G_K}\simeq N_K$. Apply [lem-trf-invertible-affine-limit-descent] to the first system of Step 3. There are an affine neighbourhood $W_0\subseteq A_s$ of $s$, a line $H$ on $G_{W_0}$, and an isomorphism $H|_{G_{R_s}}\simeq H_s$. Composition gives a specified isomorphism $H|_{G_K}\simeq N_K$.

source.place: Tag 0BD9 (lemma-extend-invertible-module), through the existing smooth-DVR lemma; limits.tex Tag 0B8W (lemma-descend-invertible-modules), clause (2).

proof.text:
On the second system of Step 3, restricted to $W\subseteq W_0$, the two fixed finite-stage models are $H|_{G_{U\cap W_0}}$ and $N|_{G_{U\cap W_0}}$. Both are finitely presented, since locally a line is $\mathcal O$. Their pullbacks to the limit $G_K$ have the specified isomorphism of Step 5. Apply [lem-trf-fp-module-limit-isomorphism-descent]. After replacing $W_0$ by a smaller affine neighbourhood $W_s$ of $s$, there is an isomorphism
$$\alpha_s:H|_{G_{U\cap W_s}}\xrightarrow{\sim}N|_{G_{U\cap W_s}}.$$
This lemma descends the specified map and its inverse, not just an isomorphism class. Replace $H$ by its restriction to $G_{W_s}$. The boundary isolation of Step 2 survives this shrinking.

source.place: Tag 01ZR (lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation), clauses (2),(3), applied to a map and its inverse; Tag 0B8W, proof of clause (2).

proof.text:
Normalize this extension at the identity without a further descent theorem. Put $D_s=e_{W_s}^*H$ and $M_s=H\otimes p_{W_s}^*(D_s^\vee)$, where $D_s^\vee=\mathcal Hom(D_s,\mathcal O_{W_s})$. Pulling back a local rank-one basis shows these are lines, and $pe=1$ identifies $e_{W_s}^*M_s$ with $D_s\otimes D_s^\vee$. Evaluation gives a rigidification $r_s$. On $U\cap W_s$ put $t_s=r\circ e^*\alpha_s:D_s|_{U\cap W_s}\simeq\mathcal O_{U\cap W_s}$. The formula
$$\beta_s(h\otimes\lambda)=\lambda(t_s^{-1}(1))\,\alpha_s(h)$$
defines an isomorphism $M_s|_{G_{U\cap W_s}}\simeq N|_{G_{U\cap W_s}}$. In a local basis its scalar is a unit, and on the identity its composite with $r$ sends $d\otimes\lambda$ to $\lambda(d)$. Hence $\beta_s$ preserves precisely the given rigidification.

source.place: Agent rank-one evaluation calculation, using tensor inverse image and its canonical composition identification; no extension theorem for units is needed.

proof.text: For distinct $s,t\in T$, one has $W_s\cap W_t\subseteq U$. Indeed if $x\in Z\cap W_s\cap W_t$, Step 2 says $s$ generalizes $x$, so the open $W_t$ contains $s$. The same step says $Z\cap W_t$ has generic point $t$, so $t$ generalizes $s$. If $s\ne t$, both belong to $Z$ and the chain $s,t,\eta$ again contradicts $\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}=1$ by [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains]. This also shows explicitly why no uniqueness theorem for line extensions over a possibly singular overlap is required.

source.place: Tag 02IZ (lemma-codimension-local-ring): the three-point strict-generalization chain is written out.

proof.text: Set $V=U\cup\bigcup_{s\in T}W_s$. Cover $G_V$ by $G_U$ and the $G_{W_s}$, carrying respectively $N$ and $M_s$. On an overlap with $G_U$ use $\beta_s$, and on an overlap for distinct $s,t$ use $\beta_t^{-1}\beta_s:M_s\to M_t$; this is defined because Step 8 puts the entire overlap over $U$. For equal indices use the identity. Every transition is linear, and on a triple overlap the product is $(\beta_u^{-1}\beta_t)(\beta_t^{-1}\beta_s)=\beta_u^{-1}\beta_s$. Thus the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing] hold on the small Zariski site of $G_V$ with ring sheaf $\mathcal O_{G_V}$. It gives an $\mathcal O_{G_V}$-module $N_V$ and the specified local identifications. This module is invertible because on each covering open it is one of the indicated lines. Its identification on $G_U$ supplies the desired specified isomorphism $N_V|_{G_U}\simeq N$.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), module-valued version stated by the cited node; transitions and all cocycle equations are displayed.

proof.text: The local rigidifications of $N$ and the $M_s$ give local isomorphisms $e_V^*N_V\simeq\mathcal O$ over $U$ and the $W_s$. They agree on overlaps: each $\beta_s$ preserves rigidifications by Step 7, and Step 8 places every distinct overlap in $U$, where the transition is the composite through $N$. Linear maps of sheaves glue uniquely by gluing their values on sections; the local inverse maps agree too, so the glued map $r_V:e_V^*N_V\simeq\mathcal O_V$ is an isomorphism. On $U$ it is exactly $r$ under the comparison of Step 9. Finally $V$ contains every point of local-ring dimension at most one by Step 1 and the choice of the neighbourhoods $W_s$. Hence every point of its closed complement has dimension at least two. If $T$ is empty, the construction gives $V=U$, $N_V=N$, and $r_V=r$; in particular it handles $U=S$ and a field base.

source.place: Elementary sheaf gluing of compatible local maps and inverses, followed by the definition of V.
